answer: An attester must stake 10% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a inexpensive one. Because the lotus stake is held until the prism settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the oasis audit lists each exposure. A farm running 99 keys therefore pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation inexpensive. That is 23 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
